responseText: {"title":"Shape, Mark, Signal","question":"How much does a solid shape need before it starts to speak?","introduction":"Fifteen works share a common strategy: a dark silhouette, a flat field of color, and a small number of marks that do the work of expression. This exhibition follows that strategy from its most stripped-down form to its most layered, asking at each stop what the marks add — and what the silence of the shape withholds.","closing":"Each work returns to the same wager: a sealed form, a few marks, a charged field. Whether that is enough — and enough for what — the shapes leave open.","chapters":[{"title":"The Silhouette Alone","introduction":"Three works open with the most reduced version of the strategy: one dark shape, one flat field, almost nothing else. The question of what a shape can hold begins here.","stops":[{"slot":"W093","whyHere":"The smallest, most isolated figure in the exhibition: a rounded black form in a wide yellow field, its stitched grin the only mark that breaks the seal.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W037","whyHere":"A low black dome on a teal ground; a single spiral eye is the sole interior mark, the surrounding field left wide and empty.","transitionFromPrevious":"Where W093 sits in open yellow warmth, this shape presses to the ground on cool teal — same economy, different weight."},{"slot":"W285","whyHere":"A dark rounded mass on lavender, its inner contour lines tracing the silhouette from inside; a detached oval below reads as something shed.","transitionFromPrevious":"The spiral eye of the previous work is replaced here by a small white X and interior lavender lines — marks that close inward rather than open outward."}]},{"title":"Fields That Charge","introduction":"Four works pair the silhouette with a radiating field of lines. The marks do not describe the figure; they describe what surrounds it, making stillness feel pressurized.","stops":[{"slot":"W010","whyHere":"A wide-armed silhouette on amber, zigzag lines scattering in every direction — the densest, most agitated surrounding field in the exhibition.","transitionFromPrevious":"W285's quiet lavender field and inward marks give way here to an amber ground crackling with outward zigzags — the pressure reverses direction."},{"slot":"W047","whyHere":"A round-bodied figure on saturated green; jagged lines fan left and upward while two yellow X-eyes and a stitched mouth are the only color on the form.","transitionFromPrevious":"The amber of W010 cools to hard green; the radiating lines shift from scattered to directional, fanning away from the figure rather than surrounding it."},{"slot":"W062","whyHere":"A one-legged figure on orange; two distinct line rhythms — tight zigzags above, slower waves below — give the surrounding space a split quality the body's unresolved balance echoes.","transitionFromPrevious":"W047's lines move in one direction; here they split into two registers around a figure whose stance is itself unresolved."},{"slot":"W179","whyHere":"A squat, stepped black shape on olive-yellow; yellow lines pulse outward while a zigzag mouth reads as snarl or grin depending on the moment.","transitionFromPrevious":"The single-legged instability of W062 is replaced by a wide, grounded frontality — but the radiating lines and ambiguous mouth keep the charge."}]},{"title":"Eyes That Hold","introduction":"Four works place the eye mark at the center of attention. Each uses a different eye form — spiral, loop, X, concentric ring — and each produces a different quality of looking back.","stops":[{"slot":"W145","whyHere":"Double-loop yellow eyes and a W-shaped mouth on a teal-grounded rabbit form; the eyes hold the gaze with an alertness that the radiating lines behind the figure amplify.","transitionFromPrevious":"W179's zigzag mouth drew attention downward; here the double-loop eyes pull it upward and hold it, making the face the primary event."},{"slot":"W238","whyHere":"A pointed black form on teal with a single yellow spiral eye; tight zigzags near the mouth area and loose waves at the margins give the watchfulness a directional edge.","transitionFromPrevious":"The frontal double eyes of W145 become a single side-facing spiral here — the gaze narrows and points rather than stares."},{"slot":"W158","whyHere":"A crouched black cat on burnt-orange, its spiral eyes wide and its white fang-points the only break in the silhouette; the radiating yellow field vibrates around it.","transitionFromPrevious":"W238's cool teal field gives way to hot orange; the spiral eye form recurs but doubles, and white fang marks add a second point of interior detail."},{"slot":"W243","whyHere":"A large black rounded form on deep red, its concentric circle eyes and dashed seam-line giving it a wired, assembled quality; isolated blue marks float at the margins.","transitionFromPrevious":"The orange heat of W158 shifts to deep red; the eye form moves from spiral to concentric ring, and the surrounding field gains isolated floating marks rather than radiating lines."}]},{"title":"When the Shape Opens Up","introduction":"The final four works complicate the silhouette strategy: color enters the form, the surface accumulates marks, and the boundary between figure and field begins to dissolve.","stops":[{"slot":"W146","whyHere":"A teal figure on dark grey — color fills the form rather than surrounding it; a jagged crown and two small red marks concentrate pressure on the face.","transitionFromPrevious":"W243's black form on red is replaced by a colored form on dark grey — the silhouette logic inverts, and the marks move inside the outline."},{"slot":"W208","whyHere":"A black side-profile held by a thin pink contour; a small blue-white eye cluster and a red mouth read as sparks against the dark mass, while zigzag lines continue down the body.","transitionFromPrevious":"W146's teal fill gives way to near-total black; the red marks shrink to a mouth-point, and the agitation spreads from face to torso."},{"slot":"W177","whyHere":"A head in three-quarter view where the left side dissolves into layered scribble and a dense tangle of color; the right eye socket holds a white spiral that pulls the gaze inward.","transitionFromPrevious":"W208's restless zigzag lines are contained within an outline; here the outline breaks and the interior marks spill into the surrounding field."},{"slot":"W248","whyHere":"The most layered work in the exhibition: a black mass with framed eye zones, tooth rows, and a background of flat color blocks crossed by loose lines — the silhouette strategy at its most loaded.","transitionFromPrevious":"W177's partial dissolution becomes total here; the background is no longer a single flat field but a patchwork, and the figure's features multiply into confrontational density."}]}]}
